desc:
Simulate a stack-like container. You are given a list of operations ops, where each operation is a pair:

  • [1, x]: push the value x.
  • [0, 0]: pop. Remove and report the value that occurs most often in the container. If several values are tied for most occurrences, remove the one whose most recent push is the latest, i.e. the one closest to the top. Exactly one copy (its most recently pushed one) is removed.

Return the values reported by the pop operations, in order. A pop is only given when the container is not empty.

For example, pushing 5, 7, 5, 7, 4, 5 and then popping four times returns [5, 7, 5, 4].
constraints: Each operation is [1, x] with -10<sup>9</sup> ≤ x ≤ 10<sup>9</sup>, or [0, 0]
Every pop happens while the container holds at least one value
hints: Simulating each pop by scanning the whole container is O(n) per pop. You need the answer in about O(1).
Keep freq[x], the current number of copies of x. Imagine a separate stack for each frequency level f: the stack of level f holds, in push order, the values that have reached count f.

A push of x raises freq[x] to f and pushes x on level-f's stack, updating the maximum level. A pop takes the top of the highest non-empty level's stack, lowers that value's frequency by one, and lowers the maximum level if that stack became empty.
editorial: Maintain freq (value → count), groups (frequency → stack of values) and maxf. Push x: freq[x] += 1, append x to groups[freq[x]], and update maxf = max(maxf, freq[x]). Note that x is appended to every level 1..freq[x] over time, one per push, never removed from lower levels when it moves up.

Pop: take x = groups[maxf].pop(), set freq[x] -= 1, and if groups[maxf] is empty then maxf -= 1. The top of the highest level is exactly the most frequent value; among ties it is the one that reached that frequency last, which is the one with the latest relevant push. The remaining copies of x stay in the lower level stacks in the correct order. Every operation is O(1), so the whole run is O(n). This is bucketing by frequency, with a stack inside each bucket.
